L24: # ACE_HEADER structure (winnt.h)
L25: 
L26: Feedback
L27: 
L28: Summarize this article for me
L29: 
L30: ## In this article
L31: 
L32: The ACE_HEADER structure defines the type and size of an 【5†access control entry】 (ACE).
L33: 
L34: ## Syntax
L35: 
L36:     `typedef struct _ACE_HEADER {
L37:       BYTE AceType;
L38:       BYTE AceFlags;
L39:       WORD AceSize;
L40:     } ACE_HEADER;
L41:     `
L42: ## Members
L43: 
L44: `AceType`
L45: 
L46: Specifies the ACE type. This member can be one of the following values.
L47: 
L48: Value  | Meaning
L49: --- | ---
L50: 
L51: ACCESS_ALLOWED_ACE_TYPE
L52:  | Access-allowed ACE that uses the 【6†ACCESS_ALLOWED_ACE】 structure.
L53: 
L54: ACCESS_ALLOWED_CALLBACK_ACE_TYPE
L55:  | Access-allowed callback ACE that uses the 【7†ACCESS_ALLOWED_CALLBACK_ACE】 structure.
L56: 
L57: ACCESS_ALLOWED_CALLBACK_OBJECT_ACE_TYPE
L58:  | Object-specific access-allowed callback ACE that uses the 【8†ACCESS_ALLOWED_CALLBACK_OBJECT_ACE】 structure.
L59: ACCESS_ALLOWED_COMPOUND_ACE_TYPE
L60:  | Reserved.
L61: 
L62: ACCESS_ALLOWED_OBJECT_ACE_TYPE
L63:  | Object-specific access-allowed ACE that uses the 【9†ACCESS_ALLOWED_OBJECT_ACE】 structure.
L64: 
L65: ACCESS_DENIED_ACE_TYPE
L66:  | Access-denied ACE that uses the 【10†ACCESS_DENIED_ACE】 structure.
L67: 
L68: ACCESS_DENIED_CALLBACK_ACE_TYPE
L69:  | Access-denied callback ACE that uses the 【11†ACCESS_DENIED_CALLBACK_ACE】 structure.
L70: ACCESS_DENIED_CALLBACK_OBJECT_ACE_TYPE
L71:  | Object-specific access-denied callback ACE that uses the 【11†ACCESS_DENIED_CALLBACK_OBJECT_ACE】 structure.
L72: 
L73: ACCESS_DENIED_OBJECT_ACE_TYPE
L74:  | Object-specific access-denied ACE that uses the 【12†ACCESS_DENIED_OBJECT_ACE】 structure.
L75: 
L76: ACCESS_MAX_MS_ACE_TYPE
L77:  | Same as SYSTEM_ALARM_OBJECT_ACE_TYPE.
L78: 
L79: ACCESS_MAX_MS_V2_ACE_TYPE
L80:  | Same as SYSTEM_ALARM_ACE_TYPE.
L81: 
L82: ACCESS_MAX_MS_V3_ACE_TYPE
L83:  | Reserved.
L84: 
L85: ACCESS_MAX_MS_V4_ACE_TYPE
L86:  | Same as SYSTEM_ALARM_OBJECT_ACE_TYPE.
L87: ACCESS_MAX_MS_OBJECT_ACE_TYPE
L88:  | Same as SYSTEM_ALARM_OBJECT_ACE_TYPE.
L89: 
L90: ACCESS_MIN_MS_ACE_TYPE
L91:  | Same as ACCESS_ALLOWED_ACE_TYPE.
L92: 
L93: ACCESS_MIN_MS_OBJECT_ACE_TYPE
L94:  | Same as ACCESS_ALLOWED_OBJECT_ACE_TYPE.
L95: 
L96: SYSTEM_ALARM_ACE_TYPE
L97:  | Reserved for future use. System-alarm ACE that uses the 【13†SYSTEM_ALARM_ACE】 structure.
L98: 
L99: SYSTEM_ALARM_CALLBACK_ACE_TYPE
L100:  | Reserved for future use. System-alarm callback ACE that uses the 【14†SYSTEM_ALARM_CALLBACK_ACE】 structure.
L101: SYSTEM_ALARM_CALLBACK_OBJECT_ACE_TYPE
L102:  | Reserved for future use. Object-specific system-alarm callback ACE that uses the 【15†SYSTEM_ALARM_CALLBACK_OBJECT_ACE】 structure.
L103: 
L104: SYSTEM_ALARM_OBJECT_ACE_TYPE
L105:  | Reserved for future use. Object-specific system-alarm ACE that uses the 【16†SYSTEM_ALARM_OBJECT_ACE】 structure.
L106: 
L107: SYSTEM_AUDIT_ACE_TYPE
L108:  | System-audit ACE that uses the 【17†SYSTEM_AUDIT_ACE】 structure.
L109: SYSTEM_AUDIT_CALLBACK_ACE_TYPE
L110:  | System-audit callback ACE that uses the 【18†SYSTEM_AUDIT_CALLBACK_ACE】 structure.
L111: 
L112: SYSTEM_AUDIT_CALLBACK_OBJECT_ACE_TYPE
L113:  | Object-specific system-audit callback ACE that uses the 【19†SYSTEM_AUDIT_CALLBACK_OBJECT_ACE】 structure.
L114: 
L115: SYSTEM_AUDIT_OBJECT_ACE_TYPE
L116:  | Object-specific system-audit ACE that uses the 【16†SYSTEM_AUDIT_OBJECT_ACE】 structure.
L117: 
L118: SYSTEM_MANDATORY_LABEL_ACE_TYPE
L119: 0x11
L120:  | Mandatory label ACE that uses the 【20†SYSTEM_MANDATORY_LABEL_ACE】 structure.
L121: `AceFlags`
L122: 
L123: Specifies a set of ACE type-specific control flags. This member can be a combination of the following values.
L124: 
L125: Value  | Meaning
L126: --- | ---
L127: 
L128: CONTAINER_INHERIT_ACE
L129:  | Child objects that are containers, such as directories, inherit the ACE as an effective ACE. The inherited ACE is inheritable unless the NO_PROPAGATE_INHERIT_ACE bit flag is also set.
L130: FAILED_ACCESS_ACE_FLAG
L131:  | Used with system-audit ACEs in a 【21†system access control list】 (SACL) to generate audit messages for failed access attempts.
L132: 
L133: INHERIT_ONLY_ACE
L134:  | Indicates an inherit-only ACE, which does not control access to the object to which it is attached. If this flag is not set, the ACE is an effective ACE which controls access to the object to which it is attached. Both effective and inherit-only ACEs can be inherited depending on the state of the other inheritance flags.
L135: INHERITED_ACE
L136:  | Indicates that the ACE was inherited. The system sets this bit when it propagates an inherited ACE to a child object.
L137: 
L138: NO_PROPAGATE_INHERIT_ACE
L139:  | If the ACE is inherited by a child object, the system clears the OBJECT_INHERIT_ACE and CONTAINER_INHERIT_ACE flags in the inherited ACE. This prevents the ACE from being inherited by subsequent generations of objects.
L140: OBJECT_INHERIT_ACE
L141:  | Noncontainer child objects inherit the ACE as an effective ACE. For child objects that are containers, the ACE is inherited as an inherit-only ACE unless the NO_PROPAGATE_INHERIT_ACE bit flag is also set.
L142: 
L143: SUCCESSFUL_ACCESS_ACE_FLAG
L144:  | Used with system-audit ACEs in a SACL to generate audit messages for successful access attempts.
L145: 
L146: `AceSize`
L147: 
L148: Specifies the size, in bytes, of the ACE.
L149: ## Remarks
L150: 
L151: The ACE_HEADER structure is the first member of the various types of ACE structures, such as 【6†ACCESS_ALLOWED_ACE】.
L152: 
L153: System-alarm ACEs are not currently supported. The AceType member cannot specify the SYSTEM_ALARM_ACE_TYPE or SYSTEM_ALARM_OBJECT_ACE_TYPE values. Do not use the 【13†SYSTEM_ALARM_ACE】 or 【16†SYSTEM_ALARM_OBJECT_ACE】 structures.
L154: ## Requirements
L155: 
L156: Requirement  | Value
L157: --- | ---
L158: Minimum supported client  | Windows XP [desktop apps only]
L159: Minimum supported server  | Windows Server 2003 [desktop apps only]
L160: Header  | winnt.h (include Windows.h)

L24: # SID Attributes in an Access Token
L25: 
L26: Feedback
L27: 
L28: Summarize this article for me
L29: ## In this article
L30: 
L31: Each user and group 【5†security identifier】 (SID) in an 【6†access token】 has a set of attributes that control how the system uses the SID in an access check. The following table lists the attributes that control access checking.
L32: Attribute  | Description
L33: --- | ---
L34: SE_GROUP_ENABLED  | A SID with this attribute is enabled for access checks. When the system performs an access check, it checks for access-allowed and access-denied 【6†access control entries】 (ACEs) that apply to one of the enabled SIDs in the access token. A SID without this attribute is ignored during an access check unless the SE_GROUP_USE_FOR_DENY_ONLY attribute is set.
L35: SE_GROUP_USE_FOR_DENY_ONLY  | A SID with this attribute is a deny-only SID. When the system performs an access check, it checks for access-denied ACEs that apply to the SID, but it ignores access-allowed ACEs for the SID. If this attribute is set, the SE_GROUP_ENABLED attribute is not set and the SID cannot be reenabled.
L36: To set or clear the SE_GROUP_ENABLED attribute of a group SID, use the 【7†AdjustTokenGroups】 function. You cannot disable a group SID that has the SE_GROUP_MANDATORY attribute. You cannot use AdjustTokenGroups to disable the user SID of an access token.
L37: 
L38: To determine whether a SID is enabled in a token, that is, whether it has the SE_GROUP_ENABLED attribute, call the 【8†CheckTokenMembership】 function.
L39: To set the SE_GROUP_USE_FOR_DENY_ONLY attribute of a SID, include the SID in the list of deny-only SIDs that you specify when you call the 【9†CreateRestrictedToken】 function. CreateRestrictedToken can apply the SE_GROUP_USE_FOR_DENY_ONLY attribute to any SID, including the user SID and group SIDs that have the SE_GROUP_MANDATORY attribute. However, you cannot remove the deny-only attribute from a SID, nor can you use 【7†AdjustTokenGroups】 to set the SE_GROUP_ENABLED attribute on a deny-only SID.
L40: To get the attributes of a SID, call the 【10†GetTokenInformation】 function with the TokenGroups value. The function returns an array of 【11†SID_AND_ATTRIBUTES】 structures that identify the group SIDs and their attributes.
L41:

L24: # AccessCheck function (securitybaseapi.h)
L25: 
L26: Feedback
L27: 
L28: Summarize this article for me
L29: 
L30: ## In this article
L31: 
L32: The AccessCheck function determines whether a 【5†security descriptor】 grants a specified set of access rights to the client identified by an 【6†access token】. Typically, server applications use this function to check access to a private object.
L33: ## Syntax
L34: 
L35:     `BOOL AccessCheck(
L36:       [in]            PSECURITY_DESCRIPTOR pSecurityDescriptor,
L37:       [in]            HANDLE               ClientToken,
L38:       [in]            DWORD                DesiredAccess,
L39:       [in]            PGENERIC_MAPPING     GenericMapping,
L40:       [out, optional] PPRIVILEGE_SET       PrivilegeSet,
L41:       [in, out]       LPDWORD              PrivilegeSetLength,
L42:       [out]           LPDWORD              GrantedAccess,
L43:       [out]           LPBOOL               AccessStatus
L44:     );
L45:     `
L46: ## Parameters
L47: 
L48: `[in] pSecurityDescriptor`
L49: 
L50: A pointer to a 【7†SECURITY_DESCRIPTOR】 structure against which access is checked.
L51: 
L52: `[in] ClientToken`
L53: 
L54: A handle to an 【8†impersonation token】 that represents the client that is attempting to gain access. The handle must have TOKEN_QUERY access to the token; otherwise, the function fails with ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED.
L55: 
L56: `[in] DesiredAccess`
L57: 【6†Access mask】 that specifies the access rights to check. This mask must have been mapped by the 【9†MapGenericMask】 function to contain no generic access rights.
L58: 
L59: If this parameter is MAXIMUM_ALLOWED, the function sets the GrantedAccess access mask to indicate the maximum access rights the 【5†security descriptor】 allows the client.
L60: 
L61: `[in] GenericMapping`
L62: 
L63: A pointer to the 【10†GENERIC_MAPPING】 structure associated with the object for which access is being checked.
L64: 
L65: `[out, optional] PrivilegeSet`
L66: A pointer to a 【11†PRIVILEGE_SET】 structure that receives the 【12†privileges】 used to perform the access validation. If no privileges were used, the function sets the PrivilegeCount member to zero.
L67: 
L68: `[in, out] PrivilegeSetLength`
L69: 
L70: Specifies the size, in bytes, of the buffer pointed to by the PrivilegeSet parameter.
L71: 
L72: `[out] GrantedAccess`
L73: A pointer to an 【6†access mask】 that receives the granted access rights. If AccessStatus is set to FALSE, the function sets the access mask to zero. If the function fails, it does not set the access mask.
L74: 
L75: `[out] AccessStatus`
L76: A pointer to a variable that receives the results of the access check. If the security descriptor allows the requested access rights to the client identified by the access token, AccessStatus is set to TRUE. Otherwise, AccessStatus is set to FALSE, and you can call 【13†GetLastError】 to get extended error information.
L77: ## Return value
L78: 
L79: If the function succeeds, the return value is nonzero.
L80: 
L81: If the function fails, the return value is zero. To get extended error information, call 【13†GetLastError】.
L82: ## Remarks
L83: 
L84: For more information, see the 【14†How AccessCheck Works】 overview.
L85: 
L86: The AccessCheck function compares the specified 【5†security descriptor】 with the specified access token and indicates, in the AccessStatus parameter, whether access is granted or denied. If access is granted, the requested 【6†access mask】 becomes the object's granted access mask.
L87: 
L88: If the security descriptor's DACL is NULL, the AccessStatus parameter returns TRUE, which indicates that the client has the requested access.
L89: The AccessCheck function fails with ERROR_INVALID_SECURITY_DESCR if the security descriptor does not contain owner and group SIDs.
L90: 
L91: The AccessCheck function does not generate an audit. If your application requires audits for access checks, use functions such as 【15†AccessCheckAndAuditAlarm】, 【16†AccessCheckByTypeAndAuditAlarm】, 【17†AccessCheckByTypeResultListAndAuditAlarm】, or 【18†AccessCheckByTypeResultListAndAuditAlarmByHandle】, instead of AccessCheck.
L92: #### Examples
L93: 
L94: For an example that uses this function, see 【19†Verifying Client Access with ACLs】.
L95:
